question: If $\vec{p} = 5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{q} = -3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, find a unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec{p}$ and $\vec{q}$.
explanation:
Step 1: Compute $\vec{p} \times \vec{q}$ using the determinant formula:

$\vec{p} \times \vec{q} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 5 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & 4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}((-2)\times2 - 1\times4) - \hat{j}(5\times2 - 1\times(-3)) + \hat{k}(5\times4 - (-2)\times(-3))$

$= \hat{i}(-4 - 4) - \hat{j}(10 + 3) + \hat{k}(20 - 6)$

$= -8\hat{i} - 13\hat{j} + 14\hat{k}$

Step 2: Find its magnitude:

$|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}| = \sqrt{(-8)^2 + (-13)^2 + 14^2} = \sqrt{64 + 169 + 196} = \sqrt{429}$

Step 3: Get the unit vector:

$\vec{u} = \dfrac{\vec{p} \times \vec{q}}{|\vec{p} \times \vec{q}|} = \dfrac{-8\hat{i} - 13\hat{j} + 14\hat{k}}{\sqrt{429}}$
